quizName: DMV Practice Test #7 15 Questions • Passing Score 12

questions.question: What is the best way to stop quickly?

options.text: Use only the front brake.
Use the rear brake first.
Close the throttle and use the front brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, press both brakes together firmly. Do not panic if the brakes lock up.

questions.question: How do you brake in a straight line for the shortest stop?

options.text: Use only the rear brake.
Use only the front brake.
Use both brakes without locking either wheel.
Use both brakes and lock the rear wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes without locking either wheel.
questions.explanation: On a straight road, use both brakes to stop in the shortest distance. Avoid locking either brake.

questions.question: Can you usually hear a tire go flat while riding?

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: You will rarely hear a tire go flat. Instead, you may notice the motorcycle handles differently.

questions.question: What should you do if your motorcycle weaves while crossing rain grooves or bridge gratings?

options.text: Stay relaxed, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.
Hold the handlebars tightly and speed up to cross quickly.
Ride in a zigzag motion.
Ride on the shoulder instead of over the grooves.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay relaxed, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.
questions.explanation: Weaving over rain grooves or bridge gratings is not dangerous. Simply relax and ride straight across at a steady speed. Zigzagging is more dangerous than riding straight.

questions.question: What does a plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protect?

options.text: It is not needed if you have a windshield.
It protects only your eyes.
It protects your whole face.
It is less effective than goggles.

questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your whole face in a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield alone is not enough protection.

questions.question: Where should you ride in your lane when being passed?

options.text: In the center of the lane.
In the left portion of the lane.
In the right portion of the lane.
Move between all three portions as the vehicle passes.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when being passed. Riding on the side near the passing vehicle increases collision risk. Riding on the far side may cause the other driver to move back into your lane too soon.

questions.question: How can a motorcyclist stop other vehicles from sharing their lane?

options.text: Ride on the left side of the lane.
Ride in the center of the lane.
Give dirty looks to other drivers.
Ride in a zigzag pattern.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane to discourage other drivers from trying to squeeze in next to you.

questions.question: What should you do if you lock the rear brake while braking on good pavement?

options.text: Keep it locked until you stop completely.
Release it and use only the front brake.
Release it, then apply it again quickly.
Release it and downshift.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep it locked until you stop completely.
questions.explanation: If you lock the rear brake on good pavement, keep it locked until you stop. You can still control your motorcycle with a locked rear wheel if it is upright and going straight.

questions.question: What helps reduce your reaction time to a hazard?

options.text: Always ride below the speed limit.
Keep your fingers near the clutch and brake levers.
Shift into neutral when slowing down.
Pull the clutch when turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your fingers near the clutch and brake levers.
questions.explanation: In high-risk areas like school zones or construction zones, keep your fingers near the clutch and brakes. This reduces the time you need to react to a hazard.

questions.question: What should you do if your motorcycle starts to wobble?

options.text: Speed up to get out of the wobble.
Use the brakes right away.
Grip the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.
Downshift.

questions.correctAnswerText: Grip the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up during a wobble—it will make it worse. Instead, grip the handlebars firmly, slow down gradually by closing the throttle, lean forward and down, and pull off the road. Avoid using the brakes, as this can make the wobble worse.

questions.question: What is the best group formation for curves, turns, or entering a highway?

options.text: Pairs.
Single-file.
Staggered.
Passing.

questions.explanation: Staggered formation is good for group riding on straight roads. However, use single-file formation when going through curves, turns, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: In a normal turn, how should the motorcycle and rider lean?

options.text: The motorcycle and rider should lean together.
The motorcycle and rider should lean in opposite directions.
The motorcycle should lean, but the rider should not.
The rider should lean, but the motorcycle should not.

questions.correctAnswerText: The motorcycle and rider should lean together.
questions.explanation: In normal turns, the motorcycle and rider lean together at the same angle. In slow, tight turns, only the motorcycle leans while the rider stays upright.

questions.question: How much of a motorcycle's stopping power comes from the front brake?

options.text: About one-quarter
About one-half
About three-quarters

questions.explanation: The front brake is much stronger than the rear brake. It provides about three-quarters of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: What lane position should you use when riding a motorcycle?

options.text: Always avoid the left portion of a lane.
Always avoid the right portion of a lane.
Always avoid the center portion of a lane.
Use whichever portion of the lane is safest.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use whichever portion of the lane is safest.
questions.explanation: There is no single lane position to always avoid. Change your position based on road conditions.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders position themselves in a group?

options.text: In the front of the group.
Right behind the leader.
At the back of the group.
Wherever they are most comfortable.

questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride just behind the leader near the front. This way, experienced riders at the back can watch over them.
